_meta.role: Staff Embedded Firmware Engineer — Platform Controller (Zephyr RTOS)

summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY with embedded firmware experience across STM32 Cortex-M, Arduino, and NVIDIA Jetson. Skilled in bare-metal embedded C, FreeRTOS, and UART/I2C/SPI, with timer-triggered ADC, PWM, and interrupt-driven peripheral firmware. Deployed quantized ML inference on edge targets: 8-bit quantization cut memory ~55%; TensorRT gave a 5.2× speedup.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

experience.title: Deep Learning Intern
bullets: Trained YOLOv8n on 1,133 annotated images achieving 83% mAP@50 on held-out validation; exported to ONNX and TFLite for mobile deployment.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.
Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2× speedup: 56.7→10.9 ms, 17.6→92 FPS vs eager PyTorch) for visual servoing with dual VL53L0X ToF sensors (gripper-ToF-triggered close at 25 mm) via TCA9548A I2C mux; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).

projects.name: SLM Compression and Benchmarking for Edge Deployment
bullets: Reduced GPU memory footprint by ~55% via 8-bit quantization (bitsandbytes LLM.int8()) on TinyLlama 1.1B; profiled peak VRAM and inference latency across prompt types using pynvml and psutil.
Benchmarked on HellaSwag, GSM8K, and ARC: <1% accuracy degradation, +0.09 perplexity, near-lossless compression.
